title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 125 (Investor Education and Protection Fund)

content.overview: Section 125 constitutes the Investor Education and Protection Fund. Amounts credited include unpaid dividend accounts transferred under section 124, matured deposits and debentures unclaimed for seven years, application money due for refund, and other amounts listed in the section. A claimant may apply for payment out of the Fund. The Fund is used for refund of unclaimed amounts, promotion of investors' education and protection, and other purposes in subsection (3).
content.glance: Section 125 constitutes the IEPF and lists amounts credited to it, including unpaid dividends and matured deposits unclaimed for seven years; claimants may apply for payment out.
content.study:
## Section 125 — Investor Education and Protection Fund

**Constitution.** Section 125(1) constitutes the Investor Education and Protection Fund.

**Credits.** Subsection (2) credits to the Fund amounts given by the Central Government, donations, the unpaid dividend account under section 124, matured deposits and matured debentures unclaimed for seven years, application money due for refund and interest, and the other amounts the subsection lists.

**Claims and uses.** A person may claim a transfer from the Fund. The Fund is used for refund of unclaimed amounts, promotion of investors' education and protection, and the other purposes in subsection (3). A claim is an application under the rules, not an automatic repayment. The section is not itself a dividend-declaration power (that is section 123).

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

examples.title: Seven-year unclaimed dividend
examples.body: Amount transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account under section 124 remains unclaimed for seven years and is credited to the IEPF. The entitled person may apply for payment out under the Fund rules. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: Does transfer to the IEPF extinguish the claimant's right to the amount?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The claim lies against the Fund under the rules; the right is not extinguished by the transfer.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 125 as a dividend-declaration power.
misconceptions.correction: Declaration of dividend is section 123; section 125 deals with the Fund and credits after unpaid amounts age out.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 125 provide?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It constitutes the Investor Education and Protection Fund, lists amounts credited to it (including unpaid dividends and matured deposits unclaimed for seven years), allows claimants to apply for payment out, and states the Fund's uses.
